My comment in the link above should explain most of the context. The summary is: /v/meanwhileonreddit mod @Genghis_Khan removed a post linking to a random internet forum, and marked it off-topic. The post garnered many upvotes, and many comments saying Genghis should be removed.

It's my supposition based on a few minutes of looking into this that it was an honest mistake, and not part of an active pro-Israel censorship campaign. I could be wrong. But one post-removal does not constitute sufficient evidence to call for the removal of a moderator, especially if the moderator is not contacted and spoken to courteously directly about the perceived grievance. This shouldn't be a kangaroo court.

I am frustrated by these witch hunts. I don't have a problem with going after someone when the facts are in, when someone has researched it and got their information straight. That's fine. But just accepting what someone else writes in a headline and following it emotionally is exactly the kind of crap that /v/conspiracy is normally opposed to. People posting on the internet deserve just as much skepticism as people publishing on CNN or FOX.
